conditions.m: generalized anxiety चित्तोद्वेग persistent excessive worry with somatic tension. ayurvedic understanding relates to chittodvega with vata–pitta involvement. yoga therapy, pranayama and meditation have supportive evidence alongside professional psychological care.

hypertension उच्च रक्तचाप (रक्तगत वात) persistently elevated blood pressure. ayurvedic correlation includes raktagata vata. approaches include dash-style dietary patterns, sodium reduction, regular aerobic activity, stress management and prescribed antihypertensives.
insomnia अनिद्रा difficulty initiating or maintaining sleep. ayurveda correlates with anidra/nidranasha. sleep-hygiene, cbt-i and yoga-based relaxation (yoga nidra) are evidence-aligned measures.

knee osteoarthritis संधिवात (घुटना) degenerative joint disease of the knee with pain and stiffness. correlated with sandhivata. exercise therapy, quadriceps strengthening and weight management form the core; topical applications may offer adjunct comfort.

obesity / overweight स्थौल्य excess adiposity measured by bmi and waist circumference. asian-indian cutoffs (waist >90 cm men, >80 cm women; bmi ≥23 overweight) apply. ayurveda names this sthaulya — a medo-dhatu disorder.

type 2 diabetes mellitus मधुमेह (टाइप-2) chronic metabolic disorder characterised by insulin resistance and hyperglycaemia. in ayurveda, correlated with madhumeha (prameha spectrum). management combines medical nutrition therapy, physical activity, prescribed medication and structured monitoring.
